name: T-64BV
origin: Soviet Union (modernised in Ukraine by the Kharkiv Armoured Plant)
armament: 125 mm 2A46M-1 smoothbore with carousel autoloader (can fire 9M112 Kobra / Kombat gun-launched ATGM)
protection: Composite glacis and turret front, Kontakt-1 ERA on turret front/roof, glacis and skirts (Bulat: Nizh ERA). Game: immune to all small-calibre rounds; 7.62x54R and 12.7/14.5 mm can only damage optics, external stowage, fuel drums and tracks (mobility kill on repeated hits); PG-7V/AT4/MAAWS/SMAW penetrate side, rear and turret roof; Javelin top-attack penetrates; frontal arc resists unguided launchers.
visual_notes: Length 9.2 m is gun forward; hull about 6.5 m
Six small steel-rimmed road wheels per side with four small return rollers (very different from the T-72's large wheels)
Low cast turret covered in rows of flat Kontakt-1 ERA bricks across the front arc and roof; bricks also along the side skirts
Rubber side skirts with hanging flaps; 81 mm Tucha smoke launchers on the turret left side
Two droppable 200 L fuel drums on the rear plate, external tanks on the mudguards, snorkel tube stowed on turret rear
In Ukrainian service in 2026: welded anti-drone cope cage or mesh roof over the turret, camouflage netting, logs or track links on the glacis, white cross / chevron ID marks

colour_schemes.name: Ukrainian army green with field netting
Ukrainian ID markings (white cross / chevrons, yellow-blue tape)
